basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 14.' and it opens '(Vers. 14 et 15.) Leva oculos tuos, et vide a loco, in quo tu nunc es ad Aquilonem, et ad'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 14 et 15.) Leva oculos tuos, et vide a loco, in quo tu nunc es ad Aquilonem, et ad austrum, et ad orientem, et ad mare: quia omnem terram, quam tu vides, tibi dabo eam et semini tuo. Quatuor climata mundi posuit, orientem et occidentem, septentrionem et meridianum. Quod autem in omnibus Scripturis legitur, hic semel dixisse sufficiat, mare semper pro occidente poni: ab eo quod Palaestinae regio ita sita sit, ut mare in occidentis plaga habeat.
